summary: Extended the existing --language-model-only implementation to Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL dense/MoE, and Qwen3.5 dense/MoE. The supported models do not construct their vision tower, take the direct language-model forward path, skip exact visual checkpoint prefixes, and inherit the existing serving-layer rejection of image/video/audio requests.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: all four initially targeted Qwen3/Qwen3.5 architecture names were absent from the language-model-only allowlist. Qwen2.5 inspection additionally showed unconditional vision-tower construction.

4 tests passed with 15 subtests: five Qwen VL architectures pass validation, an unsupported near-match remains rejected, exact visual prefixes are distinguished from adversarial non-tower names, and every affected loader bypasses visual tensors in language-only mode.

tests.what_was_measured: All modified production Python modules compiled successfully.

231 tests passed with 48 subtests; two pre-existing context-parallel tests failed because this pinned ROCm host intentionally rejects prefill CP on HIP before the CUDA-oriented assertions. No failure involved language-model-only code.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950) was visible through torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2.26015, but no qualifying Qwen2.5/3/3.5 multimodal checkpoint was available. No model inference or GPU memory-saving claim was made.

remaining_limitations: No qualifying Qwen multimodal checkpoint was available, so end-to-end text numerical parity, HTTP multimodal rejection for these architectures, and measured GPU/KV-cache memory recovery remain unverified.

The change covers the Qwen vision-language family discussed in the original issue and related implementation, not every multimodal architecture in SGLang. Other families remain gated unless already supported by the pre-existing allowlist.
Audio/omni architectures such as Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3-Omni need separate handling for their audio and nested multimodal towers and remain unsupported by --language-model-only.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
